content: If needed, the suppository can be moistened with lukewarm water before use. Avoid using petroleum jelly or mineral oil, as these substances may reduce the effectiveness of the product. To insert the suppository, lie on your left side with your right knee slightly bent. Gently insert the suppository, pointed end first, directing it toward the navel and ensuring it is placed well into the rectum. Overuse of this product may lead to a loss of normal bowel function and dependency on laxatives to have a bowel movement. Possible side effects include rectal irritation, burning, itching, mild abdominal discomfort, cramps, or nausea. If your doctor has recommended this product, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Persistent diarrhea may lead to dehydration. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States or Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using bisacodyl, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Consult your doctor if you have experienced a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks or if you need to use a laxative for more than one week. This product may be used during labor and delivery to cleanse the bowels before the second stage of labor (pushing phase). During other stages of pregnancy, it should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laxatives should only be used temporarily for constipation relief. High doses or frequent use can result in chronic constipation and laxative dependence.
